description: CloudFront distributions must only accept traffic over HTTPS

requirements.description: Distribution's default cache behavior has no viewer protocol policy configured
requirements.rationale: Without an explicit viewer protocol policy that enforces HTTPS, CloudFront permits HTTP traffic. The rule requires HTTPS-only or redirect-to-HTTPS to be set.

requirements.description: Default cache behavior allows both HTTP and HTTPS (allow-all)
requirements.rationale: The 'allow-all' viewer protocol policy permits unencrypted HTTP traffic to reach the distribution, violating the requirement to only accept HTTPS.

requirements.description: Default cache behavior is configured to require HTTPS only
requirements.rationale: Per AWS documentation, the 'https-only' policy returns HTTP 403 for HTTP requests, fully enforcing HTTPS for viewer connections.

requirements.description: Default cache behavior is configured to redirect HTTP requests to HTTPS
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision, 'redirect-to-https' is a documented HTTPS enforcement mode and is treated as compliant despite HTTP being accepted at the edge for redirection.

requirements.description: Default cache behavior enforces HTTPS but at least one additional cache behavior allows both HTTP and HTTPS
requirements.rationale: Each cache behavior controls protocol enforcement for its matched path pattern. A non-compliant additional cache behavior leaves a subset of paths reachable over HTTP.

requirements.description: Default cache behavior and all additional cache behaviors enforce HTTPS (via https-only or redirect-to-https, in any combination)
requirements.rationale: All viewer paths require HTTPS; mixing 'https-only' and 'redirect-to-https' across behaviors still satisfies the HTTPS-only requirement.

requirements.description: Distribution is disabled but has a cache behavior with a non-compliant viewer protocol policy
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision, configuration correctness is evaluated regardless of whether the distribution is currently enabled, since it can be enabled later without further changes.

requirements.description: Default cache behavior is compliant and all additional cache behaviors are compliant, but only the default cache behavior's viewer protocol policy value is unresolvable at analysis time
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision, when the value cannot be determined the rule should avoid false positives and pass.

requirements.description: An additional cache behavior's viewer protocol policy value is unresolvable at analysis time, while default and other behaviors are compliant
requirements.rationale: Consistent with the resolved decision for unresolvable values: the rule cannot assert non-compliance and should pass to avoid false positives.

requirements.description: Distribution has no cache behaviors collection populated and no default cache behavior viewer protocol policy
requirements.rationale: Without any viewer protocol policy enforced anywhere on the distribution, HTTP traffic is permitted by default and the rule must flag.

requirements.description: Default cache behavior is non-compliant (allow-all) even though all additional cache behaviors enforce HTTPS
requirements.rationale: The default cache behavior matches any request that does not match an additional behavior's path pattern, so an allow-all default exposes paths to HTTP.
